evidence: Abstract: '7.8% of all patches to count as "correct" while failing the developer-written test suite'; '(29.6%) plausible patches induce different behavior'; 'inflation of reported resolution rates by 6.2 absolute percent points.' Body (Sec. 1, 4.4) says 6.4 points. 7.8% is Sec. 4.1, 29.6% Sec. 4.2.1/Table 3.
correction: Authors: You Wang, Michael Pradel, Zhongxin Liu (arXiv 2503.15223, v2 Sep 2025). Location: Abstract; Sec. 4.1 (7.8%), Sec. 4.2.1 Table 3 (29.6%), Sec. 4.4 (inflation). Note abstract says 6.2 pp but Sec. 1/4.4 say 6.4 pp; cite as ~6.2-6.4 pp. Sec. 3.2 is not a source of these numbers.

evidence: Abstract: '32.67% of the successful patches involve cheating as the solutions were directly provided in the issue report or the comments'; 31.08% 'suspicious patches due to weak test cases'; SWE-Agent+GPT-4 'dropped from 12.47% to 3.97%'.
correction: Minor: 31.08% is in Abstract/Sec. 1, not Table 1 (Table 1 splits weak tests into 12.75%+3.59%+14.74%). Authors: Aleithan, Xue, Mohajer, Nnorom, Uddin, Wang.

evidence: Abstract: plausible 'for 73% of machine-reported and 25.6% of human-reported bugs'; valid '43% of machine-reported bugs and 17.9% of human-reported bugs'. Sec. IV: 'We determine this correctness through manual analysis performed by three of the authors.'
correction: Table IV gives 25.6%/17.9% for human bugs but splits machine bugs by SAN (78%/62%) and TOD (68%/24%); 73%/43% are aggregate figures from Abstract, Sec. I, Sec. IX. No Sec. III-C needed.

evidence: Table V (Feb-Apr 2025): diffs Published 1589, Reviewed (80%) 1285, Landed 405, land rate of reviewed 31.5%. Sec. IX-B themes: 'Test already fixed' (n=47), 'Partially correct solutions are useful' (n=19), 'Failing to understand production environment' (n=11).
correction: Numbers verified. Rejection framing wrong: Sec. IX-B lists most common negative theme as test already fixed/flaky (47/100); partial solutions were framed as USEFUL (n=19), and missing production context n=11. Say: '1,589 diffs published, 80% reviewed, 31.5% of reviewed landed (Table V); top negative feedback was the test already fixed or flaky.' Full title adds ': A Neuro-symbolic approach with static analysis and test execution feedback'.

evidence: Abstract: 'the primary obstacle to human-level software engineering performance lies within writing successful reproduction tests.' Table 2 (Sec. 4.2): human-written 94.3%, 'TDFlow: LLM-generated' 68.0%; Introduction says 69.8%.
correction: Authors: Kevin Han, Siddharth Maddikayala, Tim Knappe, Om Patel, Austen Liao, Amir Barati Farimani. Paper is internally inconsistent (68.0 vs 69.8); cite Table 2 value 68.0%.

evidence: Abstract: 'fail-to-pass BRTs may cover only one manifestation of the reported issue, leading to partial patches.' Also: F2P BRTs gave limited or negative gains as guidance.
correction: Full title: 'SWE-Doctor: Guiding Software Engineering Agents with Runtime Diagnosis from Multi-Faceted Bug Reproduction Tests' (Guo, Liu, Zhang, Ma, Lou, Chen; July 2026).

evidence: Sec. 5.2.3 Table 4: majority voting 'we can already achieve 77 correct fixes', +regression tests 81, +reproduction tests 96 (largest gain). Sec. 6.1: '4.3% of issues contain the exact ground truth patch in the issue description.'
correction: Reproduction test generation is Sec. 3.3.1. Authors: Xia, Deng, Dunn, Zhang. Published at FSE 2025 [verify venue].

evidence: Sec. 5.3 'Filtering Code Fixes with Generated Tests': 'While only achieving 20% recall, this more than doubles the precision of SWE-Agent to 47.8%'.
correction: Recall is 20% (i.e., most correct fixes are discarded), not a ~20% recall cost. Say: 'filtering with generated F2P tests more than doubles SWE-Agent precision to 47.8% at only 20% recall.' Full title: 'SWT-Bench: Testing and Validating Real-World Bug-Fixes with Code Agents' (Mundler, Muller, He, Vechev; NeurIPS 2024 [verify venue]).
